test_title: PYST 13: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 13 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A can lay railway track between two given stations in 22 days and B can do the same job in 11 days. With the help of C, they did the job in 4 days only. Then, C alone can do the job in how many days?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(22, 11, 4) = 44 units

Efficiency: A = 44 ÷ 22 = 2, B = 44 ÷ 11 = 4, A+B+C = 44 ÷ 4 = 11

Efficiency of C = 11 − (2 + 4) = 5 units/day

Time taken by C = 44 ÷ 5 = 8 ⁴/₅ days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 ⁴/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A alone = 22 days

Time taken by B alone = 11 days

Time taken by A, B and C together = 4 days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**

 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 22
 44
 44 ÷ 22 = 2

 44 ÷ 11 = 4
 
 

 A + B + C
 4
 44 ÷ 4 = 11
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B and C = 11

⇒ Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B + Efficiency of C = 11

⇒ 2 + 4 + Efficiency of C = 11

⇒ 6 + Efficiency of C = 11

⇒ Efficiency of C = 11 − 6 = 5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 44 ÷ 5

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 8 ⁴/₅ days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 ⁴/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the work done by each person. If all people work for the exact same number of days, the wages will be distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

It operates on the same logic as Time and Work. An inlet pipe is considered positive work as it fills the tank, whereas an outlet pipe (or leak) is treated as negative efficiency since it empties the tank.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, find the total work and combine their efficiencies for one complete cycle (e.g., A works day 1, B works day 2), then scale this cycle up to approach the total work.
